sections.title: Copying files and writing the manifest
sections.what: Copies the chosen files into the fixtures folder and writes a manifest of what was copied. If the tie, rain-affected match or five results are missing, it stops with an error.
sections.why: The manifest keeps the source and attribution with the copied files, which the data licence requires.
sections.watch_out: The manifest source can be a default address when the neighbouring file is missing, so check it before sharing.

summary: Copies a small, varied set of downloaded IPL match files into a fixtures folder for testing.
purpose: Creates a test set that includes a tie, a rain-affected match and normal results across several seasons.
why: Testing against every match would be slow, and the test set must include the unusual cases the code handles.
how: Reads each match file's summary, finds one tie, one rain-affected match and a spread of normal results across seasons, copies them, and writes a manifest with source, attribution, season, teams and outcome.
inputs: Numbered JSON match files in data/raw/cricsheet/ipl_json or the folder given as an argument, and an optional neighbouring source address file.
outputs: Copied match files and a MANIFEST.json in data/fixtures/cricsheet, plus a console line with the count.
risks: If the source address file is missing, the manifest falls back to a fixed default address that may not be the real download link. If a required case is missing, the script stops with an error.
debug: If it stops with a message, the source data lacks a tie, a rain-affected match or five results. Check the folder contents and the season spread.
